findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it an internet-routable endpoint (and the endpoint is exported as a Terraform output). This substantially expands attack surface for credential brute-force and exploitation of the MySQL service.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and its snapshots, leaving stored application data unencrypted on the underlying storage.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections; combined with a publicly accessible endpoint this permits cleartext transmission of credentials and query data.

The EC2 user_data script interpolates the database master password (var.password) and username directly into the instance bootstrap script. User data is retrievable in plaintext from the instance metadata service and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, exposing DB credentials to anyone with instance access, SSRF against 169.254.169.254, or read access to the EC2 API.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is configured, so IMDSv1 remains available. A server-side request forgery in the hosted PHP application could retrieve the instance profile credentials, which carry s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on all resources.

No root_block_device encrypted = true is specified, so the root volume — which persists the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file and the user data — relies on account default settings and may be unencrypted at rest.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web instance. This violates least privilege and provides a direct data exfiltration and privilege escalation path (read all S3 buckets, modify RDS, launch or modify EC2 instances) from a single web application compromise.
The RDS security group allows all outbound protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no containment against data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.

The DB subnet group places the RDS instance in aws_subnet.web_subnet and aws_subnet.web_subnet2 — the same subnets used for the public-facing web instance. Combined with publicly_accessible = true, this removes the network segmentation boundary that should isolate the data tier from the internet.
